These requirements encompass both physical and digital components that contribute to an optimized learning environment.

The work product focuses on understanding the needs of users in terms of learning resources, skills, development and delivery capacity, and capability. It also considers the environment requirements, learning platforms, tools, and channels, and how they will operate in relation to the learning program. Additionally, it addresses the technical specifications and roadmap for any tools that may impact training development, delivery, or end user devices, such as Learning Management Systems (LMS), internal systems, hosting solutions, policies, model office requirements, laptop and mobile policies, desktop setups, and cloud hosting.

Physical Infrastructure:

  • Space and Facilities: Adequate classrooms, laboratories, libraries, and other learning spaces should be available to accommodate learners and facilitate interactions.
  • Furniture and Equipment: Appropriate seating arrangements, desks, whiteboards, projectors, computers, internet access, and audiovisual aids are essential for engaging and interactive learning sessions.
  • Safety and Security: Providing a safe and secure environment through fire safety measures, emergency exit plans, surveillance systems, and controlled access to premises.

Digital Infrastructure:

  • Hardware: Computers, laptops, tablets, mobile devices, and network infrastructure need to be sufficient and up-to-date for students to access digital learning materials and online resources.
  • Software and Applications: Learning management systems (LMS), virtual classrooms, collaborative tools, educational software, and various applications should be available to facilitate content delivery, assessments, and collaboration.
  • Internet Connectivity: Reliable internet access with sufficient bandwidth is crucial for students and educators to access online content, participate in virtual classrooms, download/upload assignments, and engage in research.
  • Cybersecurity: Measures to protect digital infrastructure and data from unauthorized access, viruses, malware, and other cyber threats are necessary to safeguard privacy and maintain the integrity of learning materials.

Support Services:

  • Technical Support: A dedicated helpdesk or IT support team should be available to assist with troubleshooting technical issues, software glitches, connectivity problems, and other related concerns.
  • Learning Support: Access to learning resources, textbooks, reference materials, libraries, online databases, and academic support services such as tutoring, mentoring, and counseling should be provided to enhance the learning experience.
  • Accessibility: Providing accessibility for learners with disabilities including assistive technologies, accommodating physical spaces, and providing captioning, transcripts, and alternative formats for digital content.
  • Infrastructure Maintenance: Regular maintenance, updates, and repairs of physical and digital infrastructure to provide for its smooth functioning and longevity.
